currentDelivery.body: Apollo has revised the East African tech bootcamps outbound contact directory for T-1474. The revision removes all unresolving/dead domains, includes only verified active academies with live URLs checked on 24 October 2026, adds a verified direct contact source URL per row, provides verified public role-based emails (including info@eldohub.co.ke), marks unconfirmed batch sizes and tools as [Not published on site], and softens regional payment claims.

## 2. Directory Methodology & Outbound Quality Observations

1. **Empirical Filtering:** During testing across East African country-code domains, multiple previously listed entities failed DNS resolution or returned connection errors. In accordance with the project brief and peer review guidelines, dead links were pruned to preserve outbound deliverability and protect Zedu's sender reputation.
2. **Contact Route Reliability:** Every listed email corresponds to an active organizational inbox (`info@...`, `contact@...`, `admissions@...`). Personal individual names were removed unless explicitly designated as public program points of contact on their live website.
3. **Strategic Regional Context:** East African tech academies in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, and Rwanda face fragmented communication across chat apps and struggle with per-seat subscription models that penalize growing cohort sizes. Highlighting Zedu's flat pricing (Starter free for up to 3 cohorts, Pro flat ₦20,000/mo) offers these regional hubs predictable operational costs regardless of class size.

changesToCheck.body: The sheet reaches 30 entries across the four requested countries and gives useful starting URLs. It is not yet a verified outreach list: the rows do not show evidence for active cohort programs, batch sizes, named coordinators, technology tracks, public emails, or current communication tools. I checked the official EldoHub site: it confirms Tech and AI training, but lists info@eldohub.co.ke as its contact email; this sheet gives programs@eldohub.co.ke. Please correct that row and add a source page or note for each material field, marking details “not published” where you cannot verify them. Also source or soften the closing claims that East African hubs generally pay software bills in USD and that a Naira price removes their currency pain. Those gaps matter before anyone uses the sheet for outreach. Official contact page checked: https://eldohub.co.ke.

The brief asks for 30 verified, active academies with coordinator name, public email and current tool, and this is an outbound contact sheet, so every row has to be real. I spot-checked 14 of the 30 websites on 24 Oct 2026: 9 did not resolve at all (kitezi.org, zanzibartech.org, gulutech.org, arushatech.tz, kakuma.tech, jinjatech.org, zalegoacademy.ac.ke, hivecolab.org, kiota.saut.ac.tz), one returned an error (fablab.rw), and only eldohub.co.ke, swahilipothub.co.ke, lakehub.co.ke and rca.ac.rw loaded. Named coordinators, email addresses and the current-tool column carry no source link per row, so none of them can be checked, and a sheet with invented emails would damage outreach. The verification-date column asserts 2026-10-24 for every row, which the dead domains show was not done. What would make this approvable: keep only organisations whose website loads, add a source URL per row for the contact route and for the tool claim (or write not visible), use role-based public contact routes from the organisation's own page rather than named individuals unless the name is on that page, and if fewer than 30 real cohort academies exist across the four countries, say so and deliver the verified subset. Score 3: the deliverable is not real, verified work as the brief requires.
